Kazimierz Dolny New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kazimierz Dolny, Poland

Not demolished. This is the newer of Kazimierz Dolny's two Jewish cemeteries, a companion record to the town's separately documented Old cemetery elsewhere in this collection. Established in 1851 on land donated by Motek Hercberg, it was devastated during WWII — Germans used its matzevot to pave streets and squares, including the yard of a nearby monastery's gendarmerie post, with some local residents also participating in the destruction — and was formally ordered closed by the Minister of Municipal Economy in 1959, with local authorities demanding its liquidation by 1971, by which point only 16 tombstones remained. A 1984 restoration initiative brought several hundred scattered tombstones back from around the town, and in 1986 a lapidarium designed by Tadeusz Augustynek was built from the recovered matzevot; about 300 tombstones survive today, mostly gathered there. Unlike its older counterpart, this cemetery is listed on Poland's Register of Immovable Monuments.
